newsitem.title: UK: Gilts end firm despite more U.S. Treasury losses.
newsitem.headline: Gilts end firm despite more U.S. Treasury losses.

text.p: 1520 GMT - Gilts ended firmer despite more losses for U.S. T-bonds and a sharp pick-up in M4 money supply growth. Analysts said gilts are supported by a wide spread over Bunds, although they don't expect much narrowing near-term. * December gilt future settled 2/32 higher at 107-16

The September Philadelphia Federal Reserve survey's prices paid index rose to 18.0 percent, from 4.6 in August, further fuelling fears that next Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting will sanction a U.S. interest rate rise.
Earlier in the session, UK M4 money supply growth spiked up to 9.4 percent year-on-year, from 9.0 in July.

That took it back out of the government's three-to-nine percent monitoring range and indicated that consumers continue to spend freely. Figures from the British Bankers Association, released at the same time, showed consumer credit rose 453 million stg rose in August.
"All the data now are pointing to very firm economic recovery," said Jonathan Griggs, economist at Barclays Bank.
Griggs supported the line taken by Bank of England Governor Eddie George at the July 30 monetary meeting that official interest rates should be at 6.00 percent, not 5.75.
Uglow said gilts' underperformance of other European bond markets was providing support despite the strong data.
The gilt/Bund spread, now at 178 basis points has widened significantly in recent sessions, having spent several weeks meandering between 160 and 170 basis points.

"There is demand at these levels but we won't see much narrowing short-term with Clarke and George meeting next week," Uglow said. "There's still some negative sentiment about the potential end of rate cuts for the market to price in."
George meets Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke for his monthly monetary policy discussion on Monday.

The short sterling strip is discounting no further interest rate cuts and a quarter-point tightening in the first quarter of 1997. The December contract settled one basis point lower at 94.07 on Thursday while the March contract also ended one tick lower at 93.89.
